text:
liam: FYI - sudden spike in attach failures in eu-west3 after a partial network flap to our storage fabric. Pre-warmed scratch pools exhausted; attach-provisioner is timing out when it tries to create ephemeral volumes.

ops-bot: [alert] region=eu-west3 service=attach-provisioner severity=critical msg=attach-timeout-rate value=0.08 baseline=0.002

zoe: any infra changes? I didn't see any kernel or janitor rollouts.

omar: network team confirmed a fabric route churn at 09:41UTC that lasted ~3m and caused transient disconnects to a slice of NVMe controllers. Many hosts' janitor retries piled up, increasing background writes once connectivity resumed.

liam: that cascade makes sense: backlog writes -> scrub reclaim -> hot_pool pressure -> prewarm consumption. We should enable cross-pool fallback so scheduler can route to pre-warmed in nearby AZ rather than fail attach.

planner-bot: [info] cross-az-fallback feature flag is currently disabled for eu-west3.

zoe: flip it? there are implications for data-locality but better than customer-facing timeouts.

omar: short-term steps: 1) enable cross-az-fallback for scheduling in eu-west3, 2) throttle janitor reclaim concurrency, 3) run a targeted unpreserve on nodes that have massive preserve counts.

liam: commands I'll run: `rvctl svc config set scheduler --region eu-west3 --cross-az-fallback=enabled --apply-immediately` and `rvctl svc config set janitor --region eu-west3 --concurrency=1 --apply-immediately`.

ops-bot: [info] config-change queued by liam for scheduler/eu-west3 and janitor/eu-west3

support-ops: customers reporting Dedicated attach errors in eu-west3; sending proactive banner that we're failing over to nearby AZs for attach operations.

(4m later)

ops-bot: [metric] eu-west3 prewarm_pool_free=0 -> 48GB after cross-az-fallback; attach_timeout_rate reduced 0.08 -> 0.011

zoe: good delta. But we still see hot_pool_writeback spikes on a handful of older hosts. I recommend flagging hosts with high write amplification and scheduling replacement out of band.

omar: agreed. I'll tag hosts with device_age>1200TBW and high write_queue_depth for manual replacement. Replacement cost estimate: ~23 nodes -> +$5.1k churn if we do immediate replacement.

liam: for now we'll continue cross-az-fallback + janitor throttle. Long-term action items: 1) add fabric-route-churn detection to ops-bot so we can preemptively reduce reclaim, 2) add a janitor preflight that estimates iops delta and refuses aggressive runs when fabric-reconnect just happened, 3) enable pre-warm pool autoscaling and pre-warmed spillover to neighboring AZs, 4) tag device age and reduce janitor concurrency on hosts above threshold.

zoe: also add a scheduler-aware affinity that prefers nodes with lower recent reclaim activity when binding scratch. reduces tail latencies.

support-ops: message to tenants: "We observed a transient storage fabric route churn in eu-west3 which exhausted pre-warm scratch capacity and caused attach timeouts. We enabled cross-AZ fallbacks and throttled background reclaim; attach latency is improving and we expect full recovery within 45 minutes."

liam: logging ticket now with timeline, rvctl commands, host list, and cost tradeoffs. Monitoring for 1h. Will reopen if attach_timeout_rate > 0.02. :coffee:
